newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-BECKER SURPRISES HIMSELF WITH IMPRESSIVE FORM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER SURPRISES HIMSELF WITH IMPRESSIVE FORM.

text.p: Australian Open champion Boris Becker proved he is back to his best form after a serious wrist injury with an impressive 6-4 6-3 victory over Michael Chang in the Stuttgart Open semifinals on Saturday.

Becker played some superb tennis from the front and the back of the court against the world number two to move towards a fascinating showdown with Pete Sampras in Sunday's final of the prestigious tournament.
In the first semifinal world number one Sampras stretched his unbeaten run to 21 matches with a comfortable 6-3 6-4 victory over unseeded Dutchman Jan Siemerink.
Becker was forced to abandon his campaign at this year's Wimbledon, his favourite tournament, after hurting his wrist and still needs painkillers for the injury.
The three-times Wimbledon champion, who dropped his first service game of the week in the first set against Chang, said he had surprised himself with his performances.
"That it (my form) has come so quickly has surprised me more than anybody else in this room," Becker told reporters afterwards. "I have dropped my serve once this week. That is a record for me."
Becker came to Germany this week needing some good results to make sure of a place at next month's season-ending world championship which is also being held on his home turf in Hanover.

The three-times Wimbledon champion, who won the world title last year, has played out of his skin in front of his fanatical home fans and is now almost certain of a place in the Hanover event which brings together the top eight players in the world.
First comes the clash with Sampras, a repeat of the 1995 Wimbledon final which the American won in four sets.

Sampras knows that Becker is a formidable opponent on his home soil although the American won their last clash in straight sets at the world championship in Frankfurt last year. Becker has not beaten him for nearly two years.
"He is going to be tough to beat, especially indoors," Sampras said. "Add the crowd to that and he seems to thrive on that. He is one of the best indoor players I have ever played."

Becker added: "It is an honour for me to play him. I have more respect for him than any other player. He is a mate. In a tight Wimbledon final you see the character of a player. There has never been any disputes between us on and off the court."
Chang, the second seed, played some blistering returns to Becker's feet at times. But Becker served superbly and hit some superb groundstrokes as well to the delight of the 7,000 crowd.
Sampras, who has won his last three tournaments including the U.S. Open and is unbeaten indoors this year, took 79 minutes to clinch his place in the final.
The winning streak is the second longest of his career. In 1994 the 25-year-old American won 29 consecutive matches.
